## Natural history notes

A large sphinx moth characterized by gray to brown forewings with wavy dark lines, a stout body, and rapid powerful flight typical of hawk moths. In Florida, the Elm Sphinx is found in hardwood forests, hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and wooded neighborhoods where host trees such as elm, hackberry, birch, and related hardwoods occur. Adults are nocturnal and may visit flowers or come to lights, while the large hornworm caterpillars feed on tree leaves and later pupate in the soil.
